## 1.1

## Motion in One Dimension

Kinematics describes motion without asking what causes it. Position $x(t)$ changes with time.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## ■ Displacement

The displacement is $\Delta x = x_f - x_i$, which can be negative.

EXAMPLE 1 A car moves from $x = 2$ m to $x = 9$ m. Find the displacement.

## SOLUTION

$$
\Delta x = 9 - 2 = 7 \text{ m}
$$

## Velocity and Acceleration

The average velocity over an interval is the displacement divided by the elapsed time.

|  |  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

EXAMPLE 2 A runner covers 100 m in 12.5 s. Find the average velocity.

## SOLUTION

The average velocity is $100 / 12.5 = 8$ m/s.
